text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data—examples with known answers—to build a model. For instance, you might show the computer thousands of photos labeled "cat" or "dog." The model then learns patterns from these examples. Once trained, it can make predictions on new, unseen photos, deciding whether each one shows a cat or a dog. The accuracy of these predictions depends on the quality and amount of training data. Better data usually means more reliable predictions, but the model is never perfect.
